subject: PrivGPU fabric readiness & capacity/network acceptance checklist

Subject: Prod cutover: private GPU fabric capacity and network acceptance

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We're lining up the private deployment (VPC peering + cross-connect) for our inference cluster and need a concise acceptance checklist from Redwood for two things before our procurement sign-off:

1) Throughput targets (tokens/sec and sustained QPS) for the 8x A100 equivalent slab we plan to reserve. Prefer a number for 95th pct sustained and a conservative peak headroom.
2) Network constraints/expectations: cross-connect throughput, MTU recommendations, egress URL/IPs to allow, and any special ingress shaping.

We also need a short mutual action plan (MAP) showing who will validate cache warmups, KV cache priming, and warm pool allocation during cutover. Procurement wants these items documented before the contract executes.

Can you provide numbers and a short ops checklist by EOD Friday (our timezone)? We're targeting cutover the week of Jul 22.

Attachments: initial demand profile (attached).

—Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Infra Ops, Acme Robotics

Sam —

Thanks — noted. High level answers below; attaching a runnable calculator (privgpu_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx) and a network checklist. I'm on PTO Mon but will coordinate async; Jonas will own network validation.

Quick numbers (8x A100 equiv slab = 8 GPUs serving model M-v2, median seq len 64, 95th pct request size ~ 120 tokens):
- Sustained (95th pct across 15m window): ~1.6k tokens/sec (aggregate across slab) — equivalent to ~450 concurrent short-chat QPS (avg 100 tokens/response)
- Conservative peak headroom (burst absorb for 5m): +60% (target capacity: 2.6k tokens/sec)
- Cold-start amortized: expect 35–50% lower throughput for first 10–15 minutes for cold caches; plan warm-pool pre-warming.

Network expectations:
- Minimum cross-connect: 25 Gbps dedicated (we recommend 40 Gbps if you expect heavy embeddings/large-context ops).
- MTU: 9000 (jumbo frames) supported end-to-end for best latency under batching; provide a fallback path if ON-PREM switches do not support jumbo frames.
- Egress: allow to the following Redwood control plane endpoints (for telemetry and config): telemetry.redwood.ai:443, config.redwood.ai:443; for model weights sync (if using private mirrors) allow S3 endpoint: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (or your mirror host).
- Network policing: Shape per-tenant to maintain per-GPU fair share; we recommend a 95th percentile policing window of 1 minute for admission control.

Ops checklist (short):
- Validate cross-connect throughput and end-to-end MTU. (Acme infra)
- Reserve warm pool of 1 slab (8 GPUs) for cutover and run cache priming job — Redwood to provide scripts. (shared)
- Run synthetic throughput test at 75%, 90%, 110% of targeted sustained. Capture p95 latency and token/sec. (joint)
- Confirm KV cache TTLs and prefix caching targets. (Redwood: default TTLs are in the attached doc)

Next steps: Jonas, can you confirm the cross-connect sizing tests and add any packet-level expectations? Marissa / Laura — can you confirm commercial MAP items (MAP doc link) and procurement sign-off triggers?

Attachments: privgpu_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx; network_diagram_v2.png

Best,
Rafael

Rafael / Sam —

Quick tech addendum from the network team after looking at Acme's topology:

- Link and Sizing:
  * 25 Gbps will satisfy token throughput for the baseline profile, but if you run large-batch embeddings concurrently expect to saturate. Recommend 40 G for safety if you ever run heavy offline batches during business hours.
  * Cross-connect test: run iperf3 with parallel streams (16) for 10 minutes and capture retransmits; target <0.5% retransmit.

- MTU and fragmentation:
  * Enable MTU 9000 on the path between inference hosts and the aggregation switch. If any hop is legacy (MTU < 1500), enable IP fragmentation handling on the aggregation layer to avoid path MTU blackholes.

- Latency / jitter targets for QPS SLOs:
  * p95 remote RTT budget for model RPCs: <8 ms inside your colo/region.
  * Jitter budget: p95 jitter <4 ms — anything higher will impact batching efficiency and observed token/sec.

- Warm-pool priming and KV cache:
  * We provide a priming script that will push prefixes and synthetic requests to reach 80% cache hit rate before traffic cutover. Priming should run over 20–30 minutes for the slab size you've requested.

- Acceptance tests to run during cutover runbook:
  1) Bandwidth: sustained iperf3 >= requested across 10m window.
  2) Token throughput: synthetic load at 90% sustained for 15m with p95 latency under your SLO target.
  3) Failover: simulate single-GPU loss and confirm degraded throughput matches expected (roughly -12.5% per lost GPU, with tail latency under 2x).

I'll add a small script bundle to the Drive link for iperf3 orchestration and the priming job.

—Jonas
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
